extracted.intended_audience: NLP/AI researchers and practitioners working on creative-writing generation and evaluation with LLMs
extracted.subtask_short: LLM blind peer-review for creative writing
extracted.subtask_description: A multi-agent, blind peer-review framework for improving creative-writing generation from LLMs, plus a paired evaluation dataset (SciFi-100) that combines LLM-judging, human annotation, and rule-based novelty metrics. The work targets methods for producing and rigorously evaluating creative fiction outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blind Peer Review (framework)
rubrics_metrics.description: Blind Peer Review: agents exchange targeted feedback while revising independently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implements a peer-review-inspired workflow in which reviewing agents provide feedback without revealing identities or original drafts, and writers (agents) revise independently; designed to preserve divergent creative trajectories while enabling cross-agent critique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Targeted feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Agents exchange targeted feedback (as opposed to wholesale rewriting).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Feedback should be specific and actionable—targeting particular weaknesses or suggestions—so that the recipient can revise autonomously; the abstract emphasizes targeted feedback as a core aspect of the framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent revision
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors/agents revise independently after receiving feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revisions are performed independently to avoid direct copying or convergence; this independence is intended to maintain creative diversity and prevent homogenization resulting from interactive processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve divergent creative trajectories / avoid content homogenization
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid content homogenization caused by multi-agent interaction; preserve divergent creative trajectories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper notes that multi-agent frameworks can paradoxically hinder creativity by inducing content homogenization; a good framework should be judged on its ability to maintain diverse outcomes rather than collapsing to similar outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigorous evaluation via a unified framework
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a unified, multi-pronged evaluation framework to assess creative-writing outputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors propose combining automated LLM-based scoring, human annotation, and rule-based novelty metrics to enable rigorous evaluation; evaluations should not rely on a single signal but integrate multiple complementary metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: LLM-as-a-judge scoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Automated scoring where LLMs act as judges to rate writing outputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the unified SciFi-100 evaluation pipeline; LLM-judges provide scalable automatic scores which are combined with human and rule-based measures for assessment (details in full paper).

rubrics_metrics.name: Human annotation
rubrics_metrics.description: Human judgments/annotations of creative-writing quality and attributes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Human annotators provide ground-truth or complementary evaluations for aspects of creative writing (e.g., quality, coherence, novelty), serving as a key component alongside automated metrics in the unified evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule-based novelty metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule-based metrics to quantify novelty in generated creative writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in SciFi-100 to operationalize and measure novelty (objective proxies), enabling detection of originality beyond stylistic or superficial differences; these are combined with human and LLM-judge signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness relative to model scale (interaction structure as substitute for scale)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether interaction structure (peer-review framework) enables smaller models to match or exceed larger single-agent models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performance should be measured not only in absolute quality but also relative to model size—demonstrating that a good interaction framework can substitute for larger model capacity and thus be judged on efficiency gains.

rubrics_metrics.name: SciFi-100 dataset (evaluation dataset)
rubrics_metrics.description: A science-fiction writing dataset (SciFi-100) designed with a unified evaluation framework combining LLM-judge scoring, human annotation, and rule-based novelty metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Datasets used for evaluation should include supporting annotation and metric scaffolding to enable multi-faceted, reproducible assessment of creativity and the effects of peer-review-style intervention.
